title: Income and Wealth Effects on Private-Label Demand: Evidence from the Great Recession
authors: Jean‐Pierre Dubé; Günter J. Hitsch; Peter E. Rossi
eligible_reason: Not a DiD. Household fixed-effects regressions of private-label share on continuous log income, log Zillow house value and unemployment (within-household variation during the Great Recession), plus AIDS demand models; no binary staggered treatment.
design_notes: Regression Demand Models/empirical_strategy_inctplus2.R: FEreg(y, X = lnIncome, lnZillow, Unemployed [+ Recession, Post_Recession, Trend interactions]) with household FE, clustered by household; AIDS_lower_level and upper_level demand systems; Pre-Trend Analysis relates pre-recession PL-share trends to subsequent income/wealth changes. Recession and Post_Recession are common calendar periods, not unit-specific adoption.
data_files: PL Share by Quality and Age/Nielsen-Data/.../*.RData
data_files_note: Household regression data shipped; Section 7 aggregates shipped with noise; raw Nielsen Homescan/RMS data require Kilts Center access.
data_provenance_note: Household regression file has no stated transformation; the Section 7 aggregates are 'original data + random noise' with changed household IDs. Not inspected further because the design is ineligible.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text/mksc and papers/mksc checked Nov 2); design taken from the OpenAlex abstract, READMEs and code. Design read from the README and the main-results code; no package code was run.
